name: Systems & Ethics — Sentinel's WOMS Rollout
description: A four-round, advanced socio-technical and digital-ethics simulation set inside Sentinel Logistics (Pty) Ltd, a fictional national South African logistics company (Johannesburg HQ, 9 distribution centres, 640 trucks, 4,800 staff of whom ~3,900 are frontline, ZAR 7.2bn revenue on a thin ~6% margin). Sentinel has bought a ZAR 180M integrated Workforce & Operations Management System (WOMS) that does not only coordinate work — it continuously measures individual warehouse and driver productivity and behaviour, with a people-analytics module. Weeks before a phased national go-live, the Johannesburg pilot leaks: staff learn the system scores them in real time and that managers discussed using the analytics for performance management and 'right-sizing.' Early frontline adoption sits at 38%, the union threatens a dispute within 10 working days, POPIA compliance (lawful basis, purpose limitation, transparency, DPIA) is incomplete, and a journalist is asking about algorithmic management — while the board demands confirmation the promised ZAR 95M annual efficiency gain still holds. Playing the CIO, you (1) read the SOCIAL system, not just the technical one — mapping how the system shifts power, visibility and trust, rather than treating it as a neutral efficiency tool; (2) set the data-use rules — purpose limitation (coordination & safety vs. individual performance vs. headcount), retention, who sees individual-level data, whether scores drive automated decisions, and the POPIA lawful basis and DPIA; (3) choose the change & adoption approach — transparency, union and worker consultation, training, phased vs. big-bang, and whether to co-design safeguards WITH employees; and (4) install ONE binding ethics safeguard (algorithmic-use charter, human-in-the-loop review, an employee data-rights & appeal mechanism, an independent oversight review, or worker representation in governance) and defend the integrated plan to a board-and-union forum. Adoption responds dynamically: trust, once lost, rebuilds slowly. The math rewards socio-technical framing, purpose-limited POPIA-by-design rules, consultation-led adoption and a safeguard with real teeth — and punishes the five classic errors: treating WOMS as neutral and rushing go-live, letting individual data drive performance/headcount decisions, skipping union consultation, writing a toothless charter, and either switching the analytics off entirely (forfeiting the fatigue-safety upside and the efficiency case) or ignoring POPIA's formal DPIA and lawful-basis requirements. Final KPIs track Frontline Adoption (%), Stakeholder Trust, POPIA Compliance and the Net Financial Outcome (ZAR M) — the ZAR 95M gain that holds only if frontline staff actually adopt and trust the system.

Your Decisions This Round

Commitment to reading the social system first: 40
Committed target adoption: 70%
Adoption is earned, not declared. A target far above what your consultation and data rules can support reads as wishful — and trust, once lost, rebuilds slowly.
Facilitator (the board, the union & a journalist)
Three clocks are running: the board wants the ZAR 95M confirmed, the union wants a response in 10 working days, and a journalist is asking about 'algorithmic management' at Sentinel. The same data can flag a fatigue risk before a driver crashes — or enable opaque firing decisions nobody can contest. The system is not neutral. Which organisation does Sentinel become — and is your safeguard binding, or just a notice on the intranet?
